title: Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
authors: Servet Ozdemir, Ping-Luen Ho, Callum Brennan-Rich, Matthew Rogers, Philippa Shepley, Ahmet Yagmur, Ismet Gelen, Sehwan Song, Zabeada Aslam, Mannan Ali, Shelly Conroy, Sandrine Heutz, Gavin Burnell, B J Hickey
abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation (0.0086 +/- 0.0002) mu_B/Mn that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of (291 +/- 2) K.
summary: This work reports on the optimized epitaxial growth of D019 Mn3Ge thin films, a material of interest due to its topological Weyl semimetal properties. The authors achieved the desired hexagonal phase by growing an initial tetragonal phase and subsequently annealing the film. Characterization confirmed the structural transition and revealed the material's non-collinear antiferromagnetic ordering, suggesting potential for spintronic applications.
main_problem: The primary goal was to establish an easily reproducible growth recipe for high-quality epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films.
main_result: The authors successfully grew high-quality D019 Mn3Ge films via a two-step process: initial growth of the D022 phase followed by annealing to induce the desired hexagonal D019 phase.
method: The study employed single-target magnetron sputtering using a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3 substrate seeded with Ru, followed by structural and magnetic characterization.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Mn3Ge Heusler alloy, which is studied in its bulk Weyl semimetal form and its epitaxial thin film form, exhibiting topological and magnetic properties.
key_observables: Weak zero-field magnetization (0.0086 +/- 0.0002) mu_B/Mn, a Néel temperature of (291 +/- 2) K, and structural transitions confirmed by XRD and RHEED.
important_parameters: Annealing temperature (500°C), Mn:Ge stoichiometric ratio (3.4 +/- 0.2), and film roughness (reduced from 1.41 nm to 0.92 nm).
main_assumptions: The structural transition from D022 to D019 is assumed to be the key step for realizing the desired topological and magnetic properties.
figures_summary: Figures show structural characterization (XRD, RHEED) confirming the D022 to D019 phase transition, STEM-EDX confirming stoichiometry, and magnetic measurements showing the weak, non-saturating magnetization characteristic of the antiferromagnetic order.
paper_structure: The paper details the growth process, showing initial D022 growth, followed by annealing to achieve the D019 phase. Characterization then confirms the structural transition, stoichiometry, and the resulting non-collinear antiferromagnetic magnetic ordering.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed experimental evidence on controlling the crystal structure (D022 to D019) of a topological material using controlled thermal annealing, which is crucial for realizing predicted spintronic functionalities.
